https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/02/eu-e.text: Menü Kereső Kallas: Széleskörűen támogatják az uniós kormányok az orosz vízumok korlátozását Külföld Márton Balázs Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Széleskörűen támogatják az uniós kormányok, hogy megtiltsák a vízumok kiadását az Ukrajnában harcolók oroszoknak, és korlátozzák a turistavízumok kiadását – jelentette be szerdán Kaja Kallas. Az EU külügyi és biztonságpolitikai főképviselője az uniós külügyminiszterek ülése után beszélt erről, amelyet az írországi Druids Glenben rendeztek. Az ülés előtt egy nappal jelentették be a német hatóságok, hogy szerintük Oroszország megbízásából kísérelhettek meg egy meghiúsult támadást a lipcsei repülőtéren egy robbanószerrel felszerelt drónnal. Szerdán sajtóértesülések szerint egy belarusz–orosz és egy lett–orosz kettős állampolgárságú férfit azonosítottak a lipcsei drónincidens elkövetőjeként. A Süddeutsche Zeitung című lap, illetve az NDR és WDR regionális közszolgálati műsorszolgáltatók egyaránt úgy tudják, hogy a két férfit a repülőtér közelében talált DNS-nyomok alapján azonosították. Kallast arról kérdezték , hogy állítólag egyikük Olaszországtól kapott turistavízummal lépett be az EU területére. A főképviselő szerint ezt a német hatóságoknak kell megerősíteniük vagy cáfolniuk, de a vízumok olyan eszközök, amelyekkel az EU-nak ártani akaró személyek a területére léphetnek. Szerdán „sokan felvetették” a vízumok korlátozását. Az ANSA olasz hírügynökség szerint Antonio Tajani olasz külügyminiszter azt ígérte, ellenőrizni fogják, olasz vízummal lépett-e be az EU területére a fehérorosz-orosz gyanúsított. Az oroszoknak kiadott uniós vízumok korlátozása már korábban is felmerült. A szerdai ülés informális volt, ezeken nem hoznak döntéseket. A résztvevők találkozóra érkezéskor adott reakcióit itt gyűjtöttük össze . Ismét szó volt a lefoglalt orosz jegybanki vagyonról Kallas szerint az ülésen néhányan azt is javasolták, hogy térjenek vissza a befagyasztott orosz vagyon témájára, mondta Kallas. Nem tette hozzá, de korábban felmerült, hogy az EU-ban ragadt orosz jegybanki vagyonból adjanak hitelt Ukrajnának, ezt az Ukrajna elleni háború végéig és az orosz jóvátételig befagyasztották , de végül az Orbán-kormány által is ellenzett terv helyett a közös uniós költségvetés fedezetével adtak hitelt. Kallas szerint legalább egy tagállamból új neveket is javasoltak a szankciós listára, amire akár 1600 új természetes és jogi személyt vennének fel – a cél, hogy a külügyminiszterek októberi ülésére megegyezzenek. https://www.cei.int/ansa/180144.text: Turin-Poland: the flight that could get business off the ground (ANSA) - KARPACZ, 11 SET - The air link between Turin and Poland has the potential to be much more than just a tourist route: it can serve as a genuine infrastructure supporting economic relations between two regions that share industrial challenges and opportunities. This was the message that emerged from the discussion on the theme "Connecting regions. Creating opportunities. How air connectivity can build long-term European partnerships', organised at the 35th Karpacz Economic Forum by Confindustria Polonia and Wrocław Airport. A bond with deep roots, particularly in the automotive sector. "Poland has always been a key player for the automotive industry," emphasised Patrizia Paglia, automotive delegate for Confindustria Piemonte, recalling Fiat's investments and the involvement of numerous Piedmontese companies in the production chain in Tychy. In the past, the Turin-Katowice flight had also helped to consolidate these ties, which subsequently gradually weakened with the slowdown in the automotive sector and the reduction in flight connections. According to Paglia, it would be strategic today to start afresh in Lower Silesia, an area that is still relatively new to Italian investment and characterised by an attractive industrial and environmental context. The flight would represent "an initial point of contact", which must, however, be made a permanent fixture with frequencies suitable for business travel as well. A connection designed solely for weekend travellers is therefore not enough: routes and services are needed that facilitate regular exchanges of managers, technicians and entrepreneurs. The connection, notes German Carboni, head of the Economic and Commercial Affairs Office at the Italian Embassy in Poland, may even be a "prerequisite" for launching structured economic dialogue. Turin and Lower Silesia are, in fact, undergoing similar transformations, from the energy transition to the industrial transition. And the major Taiwanese investment in electromobility in Poland (a technology park for electronics manufacturers, ed.) could open up opportunities for the entire European supply chain, including that of Piedmont. The aim, therefore, is to look beyond the tourist season. Alessandro Saglio, vice-president of Confindustria Polonia, is focusing in particular on Wrocław and Warsaw: maintaining certain connections throughout the year would make it possible to transform initial tourist flows into mutual understanding and, over time, into business relationships. "Let's start with flights," is how he sums it up: because a connection can give rise to partnerships between businesses, universities and people. And there is no shortage of sectors on which to build new relationships: from the automotive and aerospace industries to electronics and electromobility. The challenge is to ensure that the air link is not the end point, but the first link in a mobility chain capable of supporting people and businesses even after they have landed. (ANSA). https://www.dw.com/en/yemen-houthis-repo.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NMbG Children were among those reportedly killed in two Saudi airstrikes Image: Social Media/REUTERS Advertisement Yemen's Houthi rebels on Sunday accused the Saudi Arabian Air Force of having struck a shopping area around the central market of Taiz. The Iran-aligned Houthis said at least seven people had been killed and dozens injured. What do we know so far? The group's Al-Masirah TV channel showed footage of large plumes of smoke and a destroyed warehouse stacked with food in cardboard boxes. Al-Masirah TV also reported that children were among those wounded, citing the Houthis' health ministry. Taiz is currently under the control of Yemeni government forces, but it has long been besieged by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in the country's civil war. Taiz is located in southwestern Yemen. The escalation in fighting comes after a fragile truce between Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels broke down months ago and new regional tensions sparked by the Iran war . The Houthi health ministry accused the Saudi Air Force of committing an "abominable crime," saying it was directly and deliberately targeting civilian sites in Taiz. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree accused Saudi Arabia of launching two air raids that hit the market, adding that blood was "unjustly and aggressively spilled" in a statement posted online. The group has vowed to retaliate. The claims made by the Houthis cannot be independently verified. In response to the Houthi report, troops loyal to the internationally recognized government in Yemen confirmed that their air force had struck a Houthi depot and vehicles in the area. France sends troops as Houthi attacks threaten Saudi oil To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Saudi-backed coalition ramps up attacks after new Houthi offensive The civil war in Yemen began in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-backed government. They went on to take control of vast swaths of the country's north. Saudi Arabia joined forces against the Houthis the following year, leading an international coalition against them. But so far, Yemen's government forces have not been able to effectively repel the latest Houthi offensive. Fighting has spiked in September as the Houthis launched a lightning offensive that saw them seize Yemen's entire Red Sea coast. The rebels have also launched a blockade on Saudi energy exports to coincide with Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Renewed clashes are is under way in several parts of the country, with at least 125,000 people displaced by it. The Yemeni government has meanwhile called for a general mobilization , urging Yemenis to join the army and security forces. Yemen is one of the poorest in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c875.text: Image source, Prosecutor General's Office Image caption, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv's allies needed to take "concrete action" By Olivia Ireland Â and Â Toby Luckhurst ,Â in Kyiv Published 8 October 2026 At least 30 people have been killed in a Russian glide bomb attack on two civilian buses in the eastern front line city of Kramatorsk, rescue officials say. Authorities said three people were also killed in the village of Bilenke, part of the Kramatorsk community. Another 18 people were wounded, said Donetsk regional head Vadym Filashkin, accusing Russia of targeting buses carrying passengers to kill as many civilians as possible. Kramatorsk and neighbouring Slovyansk are part of a so-called fortress belt that Moscow is trying to seize as part of Russian President Vladimir Putin's claim to the entire Ukrainian industrial region of Donbas. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said: "This strike will not go without our response." In a post on Telegram, he said: "Russia is trying to destroy all life in Donbas, and the world needs to react to this. React harshly - exactly as the Russians deserve for all the deaths they have caused." Images posted by local prosecutors showed the burning metal shell of the bus along with debris and some of the victims on the road. Moscow is yet to comment on the latest attack. It follows a dramatic surge in Russian attacks across Ukraine and a heavy increase in civilian casualties. According to the UN, Ukraine saw more civilians killed by August this year than were killed in all of 2025. In one single attack that destroyed a five-storey block of flats in Pryluky east of Kyiv early on Wednesday, 22 people were killed, including five children. Three of the children were only one year old. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who together with Zelensky visited the site of the Russian strike in Pryluky, said the attack showed Putin's "evil intent and evil strategy". He announced "more sanctions on Russia, on the war machine of Putin, on the shadow fleet, on the oil companies, on the crypto, on the financing of the war" and told Zelensky the UK would stand with Ukraine "as long as it takes for you to prevail in this conflict". After the deadly attack on Kramatorsk, Filashkin appealed to anyone who was still in the eastern front line region to move to safer parts of Ukraine. Given the sharp deterioration of security in the two neighbouring cities, he said all public transport had been ordered to stop. The safety of civilians was paramount, and "we have no right to risk the lives of passengers and drivers", he said. Moscow has often cited the "liberation" and "protection" of the predominantly Russian-speaking Donbas as justification for the full-scale invasion of Ukraine launched by Putin in 2022 - a claim rejected by Ukraine and its allies as baseless. Donbas is made up of two regions - Luhansk and Donetsk - and with most of Luhansk under Russian control, the Kremlin is also aiming to capture remaining 20% of Donetsk territory still held by Ukraine. For much of the war Kramatorsk acted as a logistics and supply hub for the Ukrainian military, however it has now come under almost daily Russian attack as its military moves closer to the east of the city. Glide bombs in particular have been launched at Slovyansk and Kramatorsk. The bombs are fitted with winglets so they glide towards their target rather than simply fall. In late August as many as nine glide bombs were fired at Kramatorsk in one day. Kramatorsk city council described the strike as a "horrific crime committed by the Russian army against the civilian population". "Once again, the Russians have struck a location where there are absolutely no military targets," it said. Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 22 in block of flats Published 20 hours ago Civilians told to flee Ukraine's fortress cities as Russia bids to control Donbas Published 11 September Russia has in recent weeks been launching constant air raids on the capital Kyiv, with sirens ringing virtually non-stop. On Thursday, Kyiv police said four people were killed and two injured in the latest Russian attack on the city. The attacks are forcing schoolchildren out of classes into underground shelters, shuttering businesses, and disrupting public transport. Moscow's strikes on Ukraine's key infrastructure, particularly on its energy grid, are causing power outages already and are even affecting the water supply. Local water authorities in the capital warned on Thursday that pressure was dropping across the city's right bank due to power cuts. Kyiv's metro network - which millions of residents rely on - on Thursday briefly halted all its train traffic due to a voltage drop from "external power centres". Trains later started moving again - but at greater intervals, local officials said. Zelensky offered his condolences to families and loved ones affected by the latest attack and said Ukraine's partners needed to provide "concrete action through new defence packages for the protection of Ukraine". Ahead of the Pryluky attack, the Ukrainian leader had warned this week of intelligence suggesting plans for a major Russian onslaught, and in Kyiv families responded by heading to metro stations for shelter. Such warnings are for now one of the only defences Ukrainians have. Interceptor missiles are in short supply around the world, so Ukraine has little chance to stop incoming Russian ballistics. Both Russia and Ukraine have intensified long-range strikes on each other in recent months, with Russian attacks targeting Ukrainian data centres and logistics warehouses. On Thursday, Russian state-run media reported that a number of websites in the country were inaccessible following a Ukrainian drone attack on a data centre of Yandex - Russia's largest search engine. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/10/thou.text: The head of India's "cockroach movement" has been detained as hundreds of protesters descended on New Delhi on Saturday.The demonstration is the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision by the Election Commission of India (ECI).The movement is demanding the election commissioner's resignation.Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital, the group said.It said in a statement they had been taken to "an undisclosed location"."They're being denied access to their lawyers and cut off from all contact with others," the statement said.Opposition parties and other critics say the voter-roll revision could disenfranchise millions of voters and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety, saying the revision was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.Delhi has been under a strict security clampdown since Friday, with tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed to stop those seeking to reach the main protest site in the heart of the city.Authorities have closed dozens of metro stations, cancelled several trains coming to Delhi and temporarily shut down mobile internet around the protest site.Dozens of protesters were taken away in police vehicles after they tried to march to the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi, shouting anti-government slogans, AFP reporters saw.The Hindu newspaper said as many as 3,000 protesters had been detained, although it was not immediately possible to verify that number.

https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/artic.text: HOME / NEW NUCLEAR Slovakia buys out Czech stake in new nuclear project company Thursday, 8 October 2026 ČEZ has sold its 49% stake in JESS, the company formed to develop new nuclear capacity in Slovakia, for EUR189 million (USD211 million). Prime Minister Fico, right, at the signing (Image: Prime Minister's Office) ČEZ, which is majority Czech-state-owned, is selling its stake in JESS (Jadrová energetická spoločnosť Slovenska) to Slovakia’s state-owned JAVYS. The Czech company said: "The construction of new nuclear power plants is carried out all over the world under the direction of the state, which is why this sale is being made." It said the valuation of the stake was prepared by global accountants EY and confirmed by KPMG. JESS was established in December 2009 with the goal of preparing for new nuclear capacity in the vicinity of the existing Bohunice nuclear power plant. Slovakia's Prime Minister Robert Fico, speaking after the signing of the agreement to sell the stake, said: "We have agreed that the Slovak Republic, through its representatives, will acquire 100% of this company, which means that we can have all the documents and permits that JESS has at its disposal, and through these processes we can significantly accelerate the construction of a new nuclear power plant in the Jaslovské Bohunice area. "If we have a chance to build a new nuclear power plant, we must go full steam ahead and with full commitment." Earlier this year the Slovak Republic and the USA signed a memorandum of cooperation for what the US State Department said would be a "state-owned American 1,200 MWe nuclear unit". Fico said the project had been granted the status of a strategic investment, adding: "We have a huge lead in terms of preparing the territory, in terms of permits, and it would be very bad if we did not use this lead." Slovakia currently has five nuclear reactors generating more than half its electricity, with one more reactor currently under commissioning. The first two, at Bohunice, went into commercial operation in 1984 and 1985, respectively, while Mochovce 1 and 2 were connected to the grid in 1998 and 1999, respectively. Construction of Mochovce 3 and 4 began in 1986 but was halted in 1992. It was later restarted and Mochovce 3 entered service in 2023, with Mochovce 4 expected to be operating at full power within the next few months. When Mochovce 4 is at full capacity, nuclear will be providing the equivalent of 77.5% of Slovakia’s electricity consumption, the highest proportion for any country, even without the new unit at Bohunice. Fico said: "If we are to continue to be an automotive powerhouse, we need new energy sources. If we are to seriously talk about artificial intelligence, data centres and if we are to fulfill the plan that the European Commission is talking about, then no other path than the path of building a new nuclear power plant is possible." https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text: US secretary of state Marco Rubio speaks to the press before departing for France on Sunday. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/POOL AFP/AP View image in fullscreen US secretary of state Marco Rubio speaks to the press before departing for France on Sunday. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/POOL AFP/AP Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Russia Explainer Ukraine war briefing: post war ‘security guarantees’ a key focus in upcoming Abu Dhabi talks, says Rubio US secretary of state says some progress made on what security infrastructure could look like in Ukraine and Europe after the war. What we know on day 1,720 Guardian staff and agencies Sun 8 Nov 2026 20.44 EST Last modified on Sun 8 Nov 2026 20.57 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google US secretary of state Marco Rubio said some progress had been made on what the “security infrastructure” of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia, adding that talks this week could lead to further advances. Rubio’s comments on Sunday, ahead of his travel to Paris for talks with G7 foreign ministers, come as Russia-Ukraine negotiations under US mediation have been set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump’s son-in-law, will represent the US in Abu Dhabi. In an interview ‌with CBS’s “60 Minutes” broadcast on Sunday, Trump said he believed the war would end ‌soon and suggested Ukraine could emerge from a settlement with altered borders. “I think we’re gonna have it done, and I think it’s gonna happen and they’re gonna end up with a little bit different shape Ukraine,” Trump said. Asked whether Russian president Vladimir Putin was stringing him along, Trump replied: “Oh, I don’t think so.” On Sunday, Rubio said the whole time the US had been talking about Russia and Ukraine, “the one thing that’s repeatedly come up is the need for security guarantees” and what they would look like in Ukraine, and on the European continent. “I think that’s what the president’s alluding to – is that there’s been some advances made in what that architecture could look like post-conflict.” French ⁠Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Europe would be well represented at the talks. “France will be in Abu Dhabi to take part in ⁠these discussions,” Barrot told French radio station RTL. “I can’t ​tell you yet who will be ‌representing France on this ‌occasion, but France will certainly be there,” he added. A Russian drone has struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern Ukraine. Authorities say the attack on Sunday hit a former school and nearby shelter in the village of Komyshuvakha, previously targeted by Russian bombs. Ukraine said last Monday’s attack killed at least 55 people. No injuries were reported in Sunday’s strike but rescue equipment was damaged. About 50 people remain missing. Power has been restored to the Russian-controlled ⁠Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine, hours after the plant lost its external electricity ⁠supply and had ⁠to ​use backup generators for reactor cooling, the UN’s nuclear watchdog said on Sunday. Zaporizhzhia, which does ⁠not produce electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel cool, lost ⁠its off-site electricity supply earlier on Sunday after the Ferosplavna power ​line disconnected. The International Atomic ‌Energy Agency said the cause and location of the disconnection were unknown. The loss of power was the plant’s 27th such incident since the beginning of the conflict. Russia said ⁠on Sunday overnight strikes by its forces had hit three cargo vessels ⁠that were carrying military ⁠goods ​for Ukraine and two electricity substations , which it said supplied power to ⁠the Ukrainian defence industry, Reuters reports. Russia’s defence ministry said Russian forces had struck a container ship delivering ⁠weapons and military equipment to the Black Sea ​port of Odesa, ‌and another in ‌the port of Chornomorsk, which is in the same ‌southwestern region of Ukraine. According to the ministry, the second container ship had delivered dual-use cargo to Ukraine. It said a third vessel, a dry cargo ship hit south-west of Odesa, ‌was carrying weapons and military equipment for Ukraine’s armed forces. Moldova on Sunday launched a new power line connecting the country to neighbouring Romania and the European grid, to reduce its reliance on Russian energy . “For decades, Moscow used energy to blackmail us,” President Maia Sandu wrote on X. “No more. Moldova buys zero Russian gas.” Achieving energy security is a priority for the former Soviet republic of 2.6 million people, which has faced difficulties since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ue/z.text: Volodimir Zelenski a făcut presiuni asupra guvernelor din UE să-şi intensifice participarea la negocierile de pace privind Ucraina, discutând cu liderii reuniţi la Dublin chiar înainte de a fi informat despre discuţiile de joi de la Moscova dintre Vladimir Putin şi oficialii americani, relatează Politico. „Când americanii şi ruşii discută despre acest subiect, nu este vorba doar de garanţii de securitate pentru Ucraina”, le-a spus preşedintele ucrainean liderilor la începutul summitului lor de la Dublin. „Este mai degrabă vorba despre un fel de nou cadru de securitate între Europa şi Rusia”, a punctat el. Este „foarte bine că europenii fac acum parte din aceste discuţii”, dar aceştia nu poartă dialog direct cu Rusia, aşa că „trebuie să ne asigurăm că Europa devine o parte integrantă a acestor negocieri”, a arătat Zelenski. Cele două zile de negocieri de pace dintre Rusia, Ucraina şi SUA, desfăşurate la Abu Dhabi, s-au încheiat miercuri fără niciun progres semnificativ - şi fără ca oficialii europeni să se alăture discuţiilor. Guvernele din UE continuă să aibă opinii divergente cu privire la cine ar trebui să le reprezinte. Trimişii preşedintelui american Donald Trump, Steve Witkoff şi Jared Kushner, s-au întâlnit joi cu liderul rus şi se vor deplasa de urgenţă la Dublin pentru a-l informa pe Zelenski despre discuţii joi seara. Vorbind în drumul său către summitul Comunităţii Politice Europene din capitala irlandeză - o reuniune a 50 de lideri din UE şi din afara UE -, cancelarul german Friedrich Merz a declarat că a primit semnale pozitive din partea discuţiilor de la Abu Dhabi, dar a subliniat, de asemenea, că Ucraina şi Europa trebuie să fie implicate. „Mă aştept ca guvernul rus şi preşedintele rus să fie în sfârşit de acord cu aceste discuţii comune”, a spus Merz. „Vom discuta, de asemenea, cine, dacă va fi necesar, va reprezenta Uniunea Europeană. Dar aceasta este o chestiune pe care o vom discuta în spatele uşilor închise şi nu o vom face publică”, a precizat el. Şefa politicii externe a UE, Kaja Kallas, a adoptat un ton mai sceptic, afirmând că nu a observat nicio bunăvoinţă din partea Moscovei şi a insistat că trebuie să existe mai întâi un armistiţiu înainte de discuţiile pentru un acord de pace sau despre arhitectura de securitate mai largă a Europei. „Americanii reprezintă interesele americane, europenii reprezintă interesele europene”, a spus ea, adăugând că tratatele UE prevăd ca preşedintele Consiliului European, Antonio Costa, şi ea însăşi să reprezinte blocul în orice discuţii - o soluţie susţinută de prim-ministrul estonian Kristen Michal într-un interviu acordat Politico. Preşedintele francez Emmanuel Macron a afirmat că Europa trebuie mai întâi să ajungă la un acord cu privire la propriile propuneri de pace şi la viziunea sa privind securitatea europeană viitoare înainte de a decide cine ar trebui să o reprezinte. Conţinutul poziţiei de negociere a Europei ar trebui să determine formatul oricăror discuţii, şi nu invers, a declarat el reporterilor în drum spre summit. „Fără europeni nu există sprijin pentru Ucraina, să fim sinceri”, a spus el, susţinând că implicarea SUA a scăzut. „Există o oarecare mediere, bine. Dar, în cele din urmă, noi vom fi cei care vom defini şi vom decide asupra securităţii noastre viitoare ca europeni. Nu am nicio îndoială în privinţa asta”, a subliniat Macron. Prim-ministrul luxemburghez Luc Frieden l-a susţinut pe Costa ca reprezentant al UE, în timp ce prim-ministrul irlandez Micheal Martin a solicitat o „conducere clară şi coerentă din partea Uniunii Europene la masa negocierilor”, avertizând că rămâne neclar dacă Rusia este cu adevărat interesată de pace. Prim-ministrul bulgar Rumen Radev a avertizat că locul Europei în viitoarele negocieri nu este încă garantat, în timp ce omologul său ceh, Andrej Babis, şi-a exprimat optimismul că blocul se apropie de asigurarea unui loc la masa negocierilor. Subiectul urmează să fie discutat în cadrul Consiliului European informal de vineri, la cererea premierului italian Giorgia Meloni. Costa a fost de acord să aloce timp pentru această discuţie, pe lângă agenda iniţială axată pe inteligenţa artificială.
